title: Customer Phone OTP, Google Login and Protected Account Shell
outcome: A customer can authenticate with Google through Auth0 Universal Login, while authenticated Customer Accounts, Operator Users and NoorPath Platform Administrators enter only their authorized protected shell. Phone OTP remains deferred until an SMS provider is configured.
actor: Customer Account, Operator User and explicitly authorized NoorPath Platform Administrator.
modules: Identity owns authentication subject normalization and authenticated AccountId.
Operators owns operator membership, operator scope and operator permissions.
The web application owns the provider-neutral hosted sign-in hand-off and protected shell experience.
Platform administration uses an explicit deny-by-default privileged account allow-list with production MFA.
routes: Sign in -> Auth0 Universal Login -> Google authentication
Authorized NoorPath Platform Administrator -> NoorPath administration
Unauthorized or forbidden principal -> Safe access state
acceptance: The sign-in screen offers Google through Auth0 Universal Login without collecting passwords or provider tokens in NoorPath browser code; phone OTP is clearly unavailable until configured.
Only the configured Auth0 Google connection can begin the current hosted authentication flow.
Return paths are same-origin and external or protocol-relative redirects are rejected.
Missing authentication configuration fails safely without exposing secrets or accepting a principal.
Authenticated principals are normalized to one internal AccountId independent of authentication provider.
Customer Account access requires authentication and cannot grant operator or platform authority.
Operator User access remains derived server-side from active operator membership, approved operator state and explicit permission.
NoorPath Platform Administrator access is deny-by-default and limited to explicitly configured privileged AccountIds.
Production privileged identities require MFA through the selected identity provider.
Customer, operator and platform shells expose loading, unauthenticated, forbidden, retryable-error and authorized states.
Protected shells preserve existing customer discovery, operator authoring and platform publication-review entry points.
Authentication failures, tokens, OTP values, secrets and sensitive principal claims are not logged.
Responsive, keyboard, minimum-target, reflow, reduced-motion and WCAG checks pass at approved viewports.
The Auth0 tenant and callback/session exchange are integrated; hosting secrets and live callback verification remain required before production acceptance.
exclusions: Building a custom OTP service or storing OTP values in NoorPath.
Provider tenant provisioning, SMS provider procurement and Google credential creation.
Account recovery, account linking and self-service role administration.
Operator onboarding or platform-administrator lifecycle management.
Production deployment before provider integration, certification and Product Owner approval.
